headline: Mecka AI nabs $60M Series B led by Sequoia for robot data training
summary: Mecka AI, founded in 2024, collects human motion data to train humanoid robots. The funding round was led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia and Microsoft's M12, valuing the startup at $500 million.
details: Mecka AI has successfully secured a $60 million Series B funding round, with Sequoia leading the investment. The round also saw significant participation from industry giants like Nvidia and Microsoft’s venture fund M12, alongside other investors.

This latest funding round boosts Mecka AI's valuation to $500 million, as the startup focuses on a critical area of robotics development. The company specializes in collecting and analyzing human motion data to train advanced humanoid robots and other robotic systems.

Founded in 2024, Mecka AI's unique approach involves compensating individuals to record themselves performing various everyday tasks. Participants utilize body sensors and smartphones to capture detailed motion data, from making coffee to fixing cars.

The startup aims to replicate the success of data-labeling companies like Scale AI and Mercor, which have been instrumental in supplying human-generated data for large language models (LLMs). Mecka AI is applying this model to the burgeoning field of robotics.

The human-data collection space for robotics is growing, with other players like XDOF reportedly seeking a Series B round at a $1.2 billion valuation. Furthermore, established human-data platforms that began with LLMs are now expanding their services to cater to the robotics sector.

headline: Nous Research confirms $1.5B valuation, launches AI agents for business users
summary: Nous Research has secured $90 million in Series B funding, bringing its total to $158 million, and is now expanding its popular Hermes AI agents into the enterprise sector.
details: AI startup Nous Research has raised a $90 million Series B round, confirming a $1.5 billion valuation. Robot Ventures led the funding, which will fuel the company's expansion.
Additional investors include Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung, and 1789 Capital. This latest round brings the three-year-old startup's total funding to $158 million.
Its open-source Hermes Agent is popular among developers, having been cloned over 24 million times. Nous Research estimates it drives approximately 2.5% of global AI token usage.

The new capital will support the launch of "Hermes for Businesses," a push into the enterprise sector. This offering allows companies to deploy customized AI agents for multi-step workflows while maintaining data privacy and security.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Nous Research achieved roughly $36 million in annualized revenue by mid-September 2026. The company anticipates surpassing $100 million in revenue before the end of 2026.
caption:
Nous Research confirms a massive $1.5 billion valuation after securing $90 million in Series B funding. They're now bringing their popular Hermes AI agents to businesses.

AI startup Nous Research has raised a $90 million Series B round, confirming a $1.5 billion valuation. Robot Ventures led the funding, which will fuel the company's expansion.

Additional investors include Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung, and 1789 Capital. This latest round brings the three-year-old startup's total funding to $158 million.

Its open-source Hermes Agent is popular among developers, having been cloned over 24 million times. Nous Research estimates it drives approximately 2.5% of global AI token usage.

The new capital will support the launch of "Hermes for Businesses," a push into the enterprise sector. This offering allows companies to deploy customized AI agents for multi-step workflows while maintaining data privacy and security.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Nous Research achieved roughly $36 million in annualized revenue by mid-September 2026. The company anticipates surpassing $100 million in revenue before the end of 2026.
